newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA HOPES TO GET $200 MILLION WORLD BANK LOAN.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA HOPES TO GET $200 MILLION WORLD BANK LOAN.

text.p: Romania hopes to get a $200 million loan from the World Bank to prop up reforms in the farming sector, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu said on Tuesday.

Gavrilescu told a news conference his ministry had started talks with representatives of the World Bank, European Union and International Monetary Fund on a series of measures intended "to start real reforms" in Romania's farming sector.

The package, including liberalisation of prices and exports as well as a coherent legislation in the farming sector to bring Romania closer to EU standards, is vital for the country to secure an Agricultural Structural Adjustment Loan (ASAL) worth some $200 million, he said.
"The talks had a good start," Gavrilescu said. "The funds will help us create conditions for a normal farming activity."

Proposals for a new system to grant credits to farmers, to replace the present system affected by inefficiency and red tape, as well as completion of a land reform started in 1991 were also part of the package, he said.
"I think the ministry's proposals are very realistic. It's a great step forward," Tjeerd Ossewaard, a negotiator for the ASAL loan, told Reuters.
"There is a lot of interest in the West for private investments and joint ventures in Romania," he added.
Romania was once the grain basket of Europe. In 1995 it exported some 1.4 million tonnes of wheat and some 1.0 million tonnes of maize.

Reforms in the sector, which started shortly after the 1989 overthrow of late Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, had been stalled years under the former leftist cabinets which administered the Balkan country over the past six years.
The new reformist coalition government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, which emerged after last Novermber's elections, has pledged to implement the needed reforms.
Talks on the $200 million ASAL loan coincide with negotiations on resumption of credits from the IMF.
Last year, the IMF suspended a $460 million loan accord due to foreign exchange market restrictions and overspending, including in the farming sector, by the former government.
IMF negotiator for Romania Poul Thomsen is expected in Bucharest on Tuesday for talks with Ciorbea's government on resuming Fund credits.
